html:
The Ashéninka are an Arawakan people of the eastern foothills of the Andes in central Peru, in the Gran Pajonal and along the Pichis, Ucayali and Yurúa rivers, with a few communities across the border in Brazil. They are closely related to the Asháninka, and their speech forms one dialect chain with theirs.

Franciscan missions entered their forests in the 1600s and 1700s. In 1742 Juan Santos Atahualpa, an Andean rebel claiming Inca descent, raised the peoples of the central jungle against Spain, and the missions were driven out for over a century. Later the rubber boom brought slave raids, and in the 1980s and 1990s the Shining Path guerrillas killed and enslaved thousands of Asháninka and Ashéninka. Their neighbours include the Yanesha and the Matsigenka.
